PrestaShop → Shopify · Migration with two design options

Aftermarket Custom Parts — Shopify Migration Proposal

Client: Aftermarket Custom Parts (aftermarket-custom-parts.com), custom parts and accessories for Harley-Davidson, Indian and other motorcycles
Prepared by: LitOS/LitGroup  ·  Date: October 27, 2026
$2,100Option 1 — 70hRebuild the current site on Shopify, with the improvements in §2
$2,700Option 2 — 90h · RecommendedNew design and build: a fresh look for the new store (§3)
EllaTheme, free through our partnership (§6)

You want to move the store from PrestaShop to Shopify. We give you two ways to do it. Option 1 keeps your current look and structure and fixes what holds it back today: header, homepage flow, filters, product page bugs and mobile. Option 2 is a full redesign, with new mockups before we build. Both run on the Ella theme and include wishlist, compare, reviews, live chat and multi-language (§4).

We recommend Option 2. You told us the site feels dated, and the move to Shopify is the one moment you rebuild every page anyway. §3.1 explains why.

3.1 Why we recommend Option 2

1. Option 1 moves the old look to a new platform. It fixes the problems in §2, but your customers will still see the site you already find dated. With Option 2 they see a new store on launch day.

2. Most of what we found is design, not bugs. Only two items in §2 are real bugs (the missing logo and the PayPal button over the menu, §2.8), and both disappear in any Shopify rebuild. The rest is how the site looks and leads people: a thin hero title, plain product cards, a menu that runs off the screen, reviews hidden under the footer, a dated mobile header. Patching these one by one on the old layout gives a site that is fixed but not new. A redesign solves them together, in one consistent style.

3. Finding the part is the whole job on a catalog this size. With more than 150,000 products across Harley-Davidson, Indian and 8 other makes, the header, menu, filters and parts finder decide whether a rider finds the right part or leaves. In Option 2 we design these from the start around how your customers shop (by bike, by category, by part number) instead of fitting them into today's structure.

4. Your customers compare you with the big parts stores. The references in §2 (Wunderlich, RevZilla, Kuryakyn, Billet Proof) are the sites riders also buy from. When a store looks as current as theirs, a first-time buyer is more willing to order a €150 part from it.

5. Mobile is designed first, not adapted. Today's mobile layout is the desktop squeezed down (§2.9). In Option 2 each of the 3 main pages gets a mobile mockup you approve before we build.

6. You see it before you pay for the build. You get up to 3 rounds of feedback on the mockups, so the new look is agreed before any code is written.

4

Features

4.1 Wishlist and compare (both options)

Ella has both built in, so they are part of the hours above. If you pick another theme, we'd add them with custom code (15h) or an app.

4.2 Reviews, live chat, multi-language (both options)

We install and set up an app for each: product reviews, live chat, and translation for your language versions. The app subscriptions are on your Shopify account. We'll suggest specific apps once we know your languages and whether you want to keep your current review services (§5).

4.3 Parts finder by Year / Make / Model

We build the homepage section in Option 1 (§2.5). For it to return the right parts, each product needs fitment data (which years, makes and models it fits) and a fitment app to search it. That data and app are not in the hours. We'd quote it once we know whether your PrestaShop store already holds fitment data.

4.4 Ideas to consider: membership and group buying

For parts people reorder, such as oils and fluids, a paid membership or points program brings customers back, and a referral code helps them bring friends. Group buying is not a standard Shopify feature and would need an app. These are not in either option; we can quote them if you want them.

ReferenceRevZilla (another store). The red box shows its paid membership: members earn credit on each purchase.

Payment and shipping are set up by you in your Shopify admin. We guide you and verify the result, but we don't enter the credentials. They give access to your money and your carrier accounts, so they stay with the account holder.
